newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX futures stalled rally to resume soon.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX futures stalled rally to resume soon.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* Fundamental strength of gasoline could continue to underpin the markets while technical momentum is slowed by pre-weekend profit taking following sharp gains this week. * Crude is technically bullish in its own right and the market is also well supported by continuous strong demand from U.S. Refiners.

A short period of consolidation is expected for NYMEX crude and products after this week's rally, but analysts say there are no bear flags flying and expect the bullish rally to resume early next week.
"Demand for gasoline is running higher than usual at this time of year and tightness in supply may continue to buoy the market", Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives Limited said.
Analysts said the fundamental strength of gasoline could continue to underpin the markets while technical momentum is slowed by pre-weekend profit taking following sharp gains this week.
However, they said crude is technically looking bullish in its own right with short-covering against oversold indicators lifting prices this week.

Since last Friday crude has held a bullish trend parallel to that seen between July 21 and August 2 and analysts said that provided supports are held during a small corrective phase today the trend looks set to continue.
This parallel support line stemming from last Friday's $19.49 low comes in at around $19.95 today, but there is still some room to manoeuvre below this level.
Daily trading recommendations by Chart Analysis-Fuller Markets see the market ranging above June/July lows but needing a close beneath $19.60 to indicate a move to a lower trend.
Analysts said Thursday's close under the 10-day moving average measure reflected the anticipated price dip today but it stayed well above the 20-day measure leaving room for longer term gains.
14-day RSIs at around 50 percent leave market direction in the balance but analyst's remain generally bullish.
Gasoline has been responsible for gains across the complex over the past week but after rallying through resistance around 66.50 cents on Thursday prices fell back in late trade.
"Gasoline made its expected move higher yesterday but ran out of steam at 67.40 cents just below the contract high," said Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research in his daily report.

However technicals remain strong with the market closing in the range of parallel support and well above the 10 and 20-day moving average lines. Slow stochastics also continue to point the market higher.

Heating oil completes the bullish long term picture across the complex though not quite so convincingly. RSIs are creeping higher into overbought territory again and the market closed bearishly under the 10-day moving average marker.

To the upside trendline support is still just about intact around 55.60 cents though analysts said this could be easily broken down if any serious sell off occurs today. However, under this level 20-day moving average support comes in at around 55.10 cents and slow stochastic measures remain bullish.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
